articles.title: Miami se convierte en Vice City y Giannis ajusta cuentas con los Bucks
articles.standfirst: Los Heat llevan el universo de GTA 6 al Kaseya Center y vencen 137-130 a Milwaukee con Giannis a una asistencia del triple doble en su primer duelo ante su exequipo
articles.summary: Los Heat llevan el universo de GTA 6 al Kaseya Center y vencen 137-130 a Milwaukee con Giannis a una asistencia del triple doble en su primer duelo ante su exequipo
articles.body: Miami se convirtió en Vice City por una noche. Los Heat llevaron el universo de GTA 6 al Kaseya Center y ganaron a los Milwaukee Bucks por 137-130 en el primer partido de Giannis Antetokounmpo contra su antiguo equipo. El griego firmó 27 puntos, 13 rebotes y nueve asistencias y se quedó a un pase de redondear con un triple doble una noche que tenía mucho de videojuego y bastante de reencuentro. La fiesta empezó mucho antes del salto inicial. Miles de aficionados hicieron cola alrededor del pabellón para hacerse con alguna prenda de la colección que unía a Travis Scott, los Heat y GTA 6. Dentro, las recreaciones de Burger Shot y Cluckin’ Bell, dos cadenas de comida rápida del videojuego, también estaban abarrotadas. Hubo actuaciones musicales, camisetas que caían en paracaídas sobre la grada y hasta una mascota del juego paseándose entre los aficionados. Travis Scott y MrBeast estuvieron entre los asistentes. La presentación de los Heat, ambientada en GTA, puso en pie al pabellón. El tono cambió cada vez que Tyler Herro entró en juego. El que fuera una de las caras de Miami, enviado a Milwaukee en el traspaso de Antetokounmpo, escuchó silbidos durante buena parte del encuentro. Giannis, en cambio, se hizo con la noche. Dio para imaginarlo en el papel de Tommy Vercetti, el protagonista del Vice City original que acaba quedándose con la ciudad. Los Bucks llegaron a 130 puntos, pero Miami encontró en Antetokounmpo al hombre que marcó la diferencia. Y así quedó la rareza de la noche: Vice City debutó en la NBA, ganó su partido y se despidió con un balance perfecto.

articles.title: Los Nets de Jordi Fernández son un polvorín: "Puedo decirlo en español, porque en inglés no me entienden"
articles.standfirst: Julius Randle le recriminó a sus compañeros en el banquillo que "no hay orgullo. Esto es vergonzoso"
articles.summary: Julius Randle le recriminó a sus compañeros en el banquillo que "no hay orgullo. Esto es vergonzoso"
articles.body: Los Brooklyn Nets (3-11) que entrena el español Jordi Fernández perdieron 107-137 ante los Chicago Bulls en la NBA. El técnico catalán habló sobre la falta de esfuerzo de sus Nets y por qué su mensaje no está calando: "Puedo intentar decirlo en español, porque en inglés no me entienden. Así que seguiré intentándolo y buscaré el idioma que funcione. Pero sí, nuestro esfuerzo no fue bueno". "El otro equipo lo hizo mucho mejor que nosotros", apuntó. Egor Demin (22 puntos), Julius Randle (17 puntos), Nolan Traore (13 puntos) y Mikel Brown Jr (15 puntos). "Es uno de los peores partidos en los que he participado", reconoció Julius Randle, que durante un tiempo muerto no dudó en decirle a sus compañeros que "no hay orgullo. Esto es vergonzoso". Julius Erving, mito de la NBA, apuntó que "daba por hecho que los Nets saldrían muy motivados. Me equivoqué". Matas Buzelis anotó 25 puntos, su mejor marca de la temporada, Josh Giddey sumó 18 puntos, 14 rebotes y 9 asistencias, y los Chicago Bulls lograron su victoria más cómoda de la temporada. Con este triunfo los Bulls pusieron fin a una racha de seis derrotas en Brooklyn, donde no ganaban desde el 1 de noviembre de 2022.

articles.title: Pedro Sánchez vuelve a 'jugar' con Estudiantes para presentar un nuevo Bono Deporte de 200 euros
articles.standfirst: Pedro Sánchez, que se formó en el Estudiantes, vuelve a enfundarse la camiseta del equipo colegial
articles.summary: Pedro Sánchez, que se formó en el Estudiantes, vuelve a enfundarse la camiseta del equipo colegial
articles.body: Pedro Sánchez Pérez-Castejón, presidente del Gobierno de España, forjó su carácter durante adolescencia y juventud jugando a baloncesto en las frías y míticas pistas del Ramiro de Maeztu. Allí, en Estudiantes, el líder del PSOE estuvo a las órdenes de Cristóbal Cremades, Ángel Goñi... y Mateo Quirós. "Pedro Sánchez era un jugador más... pero hacía equipo. De ahí a líder hay un abismo, pero tampoco en esa época se trabajaba esa figura del líder en el Estudiantes. Eso sí, la primera persona dispuesta a trabajar y tirar del grupo era siempre él", recordó Mateo Quirós en MARCA en 2018 sobre Pedro Sánchez. El propio Pedro Sánchez explicó en el dominical 'Papel' del diario 'El Mundo' que "el Estudiantes es el equipo del instituto público donde estudié bachillerato, el Ramiro de Maeztu. Allí todos queríamos jugar en el Estudiantes y tuve la suerte de defender esa camiseta hasta los 21 años. Un equipo histórico pero modesto, que ha conseguido triunfos a base de valores con los que me identifico: el esfuerzo, la constancia, el trabajo en equipo y la lealtad. Esos valores son su mayor éxito, mucho más que los títulos que, por cierto, también tiene". "Yo quería ser jugador de baloncesto. Jugué en el Estudiantes durante muchos años y es una de mis grandes pasiones. Afortunadamente para el baloncesto lo dejé cuando tenía 21 años", apuntó. Pedro Sánchez, en plena campaña electora, vuelve a 'jugar' con Estudiantes para presentar un nuevo Bono Deporte. "Este 29 de noviembre, ¡todo el mundo votando! 200 euros en un nuevo Bono Deporte para que nada te frene. No nos estamos tirando un triple, es nuestro programa electoral", anunció.

articles.title: Vanessa Bryant Quashes Report About Teaming Up With Pau Gasol to Bid For Mark Walter’s LA Sparks
articles.summary: On Wednesday, Sports Business Journal reported that Vanessa Bryant would join a bid to purchase the LA Sparks from majority owner Mark Walter. According to t...
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Sports Business Journal reported that Vanessa Bryant would join a bid to purchase the LA Sparks from majority owner Mark Walter. According to the report, the widow of the late Kobe Bryant would be teaming up with his former Lakers co-star Pau Gasol in the bid.

That same day, Vanessa went on Instagram to debunk the rumor, saying she would have personally delivered a major announcement like that.

"Another rumor out today…I've never had any conversations about being an NBA or WNBA team owner," she wrote. "If that was true, I would announce it. I'm just over here undecided on what seasonal coffee flavor I like and over caffeinated."

This is the first time Vanessa, who has been spotted watching Sparks games in the past, has been linked to any bid to purchase an NBA or WNBA team. Apparently, she has no interest in this sort of endeavor.

Last month, news broke that Walter is looking to sell the Sparks franchise he acquired with Magic Johnson back in 2014. Bloomberg characterized this move as "another step in the dismantling of his sports-team empire" amid a federal probe into Walter's insurance firms.

According to Bloomberg , Walter is looking to sell the franchise and its unopened practice facility for $700 million. If Walter finds a group willing to shell out that amount, he'd set a new record for the biggest WNBA franchise sale (a record currently held by Tilman Fertitta's $300 million purchase of the Connecticut Sun this year).

"Brutal": Sparks Beat Writer Posts Disappointed Tweet After Team Fails to Land No. 1 Pick in WNBA Draft Lottery

Amid all this uncertainty, the Sparks had a chance to drastically alter their franchise's trajectory at this Sunday's draft lottery. The Sparks had not one, but two chances to land the No. 1 pick. Aside from their own selection, which had 2.4% odds, they also owned the Phoenix Mercury's pick, which had 1.2% odds of winning the lottery.

However, when the lottery proceedings got underway, there were no odds defied for the Sparks as they ended up with the expected sixth and seventh picks. In response, Sparks beat writer Edwin Garcia couldn't help but express his disappointment on X.

"The worst-case scenario happened for the Sparks. They had two chances at the No. 1 pick and ended up with the No. 6 and No. 7 selections. They literally could not have done worse than this tonight. Brutal."

Notably, the presumptive No. 1 pick for next year's draft is an LA native. It's highly unlikely, however, that USC star JuJu Watkins will land with the Sparks if she does declare for the 2027 WNBA draft.

articles.title: NBA Europa anunciará sus equipos en el primer trimestre de 2027
articles.standfirst: Mark Tatum confirma lo que avanzó Jorge Garbajosa en el Business Sport Forum.
articles.summary: Mark Tatum confirma que los planes del nuevo gran torneo europeo siguen adelante y da el nombre de tres grandes inversores Blackstone, Ares y Arctos
articles.body: Mark Tatum, número dos de la NBA, ha confirmado en el foro Dealmakers, organizado por Sports Business Journal, que el calendario de NBA Europa no ha cambiado de cara a octubre de 2027 y que el objetivo es anunciar los grupos propietarios de las franquicias durante el primer trimestre del año. Un horizonte que coincide con las previsiones de Jorge Garbajosa, presidente de FIBA Europa, quien durante su participación en el Business Sport Forum de MARCA y EXPANSIÓN fue preguntado directamente por cuándo se conocerán los equipos: "Le corresponde a la NBA comunicarlo. Creemos que será antes de que acabe el año o a principios de 2027". Un calendario que también da continuidad a las previsiones de Adam Silver, comisionado de la NBA, quien había anticipado importantes novedades durante el otoño de 2026. "Esta es una oportunidad que solo se presenta una vez en la historia. Solo habrá una ocasión para establecer una franquicia en Londres, París, Milán o Roma", aseguró Tatum, poniendo el foco en el atractivo del proyecto para los inversores internacionales. Garbajosa, por su parte, reconoció la complejidad de poner en marcha una competición de esta magnitud y relativizó la importancia de una fecha exacta para su estreno: "¿Me gustaría empezar en 2027? Sí. ¿Me quita el sueño que haya que retrasarlo unos meses? No. Lo que necesitamos es que suceda". Uno de los avances más significativos llega desde el ámbito económico. Según adelantó Sky News, la NBA trabaja en la creación de un fondo multimillonario destinado a financiar la construcción y modernización de pabellones en Europa. Tatum reiteró que la NBA ve una gran oportunidad para mejorar la experiencia de los aficionados en Europa mediante la creación de recintos de primer nivel, impulsados por la inversión y el capital institucional. En el ambiente, flota la posible participación de tres gigantes de la inversión, Blackstone, Ares y Arctos. A este escenario se suma RedBird Capital Partners, fondo propietario del AC Milan y uno de los actores vinculados al futuro proyecto de NBA Europa en Milán. Su fundador, Gerry Cardinale, participó junto a Tatum en el foro Dealmakers y se mostró especialmente contundente sobre el futuro de la competición. "Estoy absolutamente convencido de que la NBA acabará desarrollándose. Es la NBA, por el amor de Dios. Sus resultados hablan por sí solos y su marca también", afirmó Cardinale, quien defendió que el proyecto debe seguir adelante independientemente de las negociaciones con la Euroliga: "Si podemos hacerlo de forma consensuada, fantástico. Y si no podemos, seguiremos adelante y lo haremos", comentó. El gestor italiano sostuvo también la necesidad de construir un modelo económicamente sostenible frente a las pérdidas que, según señaló, acumula la Euroliga. Tatum, por su parte, insistió en que la NBA contempla esta iniciativa como una inversión estratégica a largo plazo. "Estamos adoptando una visión realmente a largo plazo. Esto no es algo puntual. Nos llevará cinco, diez, quince o veinte años transformar realmente todo el ecosistema del baloncesto europeo", afirmó. El directivo estadounidense también confirmó que la nueva competición contará con su propio comisionado o consejero delegado, independiente de la estructura ejecutiva de la NBA, y advirtió de que el proyecto evolucionará considerablemente desde su primera temporada. Más allá de la inversión económica, la alianza de la NBA con FIBA introduce una diferencia fundamental respecto al actual modelo de la Euroliga: el acceso a la máxima competición europea a través de los resultados deportivos. El formato previsto contempla 16 participantes, con 12 franquicias permanentes y cuatro plazas reservadas al mérito deportivo. "Unos 600 clubes tienen, en la práctica, la opción de llegar a NBA Europa. Se lo tienen que ganar. Es la esencia del deporte", defendió Garbajosa en su intervención en el Business Sport Forum de Expansión y MARCA. El proyecto de NBA Europa también contempla una reorganización del calendario para garantizar la presencia de los jugadores en las Ventanas de selecciones de noviembre y febrero.

articles.title: 2026 NBA Re-Draft After 1 Month with Major Lottery Shakeups
articles.summary: NBA teams don't order their draft boards based on which rookies will look best after their first month. The way to "win" the draft is to take the player who'll have the best career. The 2026 class is still on the first sentence of the first chapter.
articles.body:
NBA teams don't order their draft boards based on which rookies will look best after their first month. The way to "win" the draft is to take the player who'll have the best career. The 2026 class is still on the first sentence of the first chapter.

Still, this is as good a time as any to make some early observations about this year's rookies with a re-draft. We'll lean heavily on pre-draft priors and potential while also acknowledging how present performance is changing our opinions.

We're not considering team fit. We're treating the draft order as if all the trades that shook it up still happened. That way, fans can compare who their team actually picked against who they could have selected with the benefit of hindsight.

Let's see how things have changed with a month of information on AJ Dybantsa, Yaxel Lendeborg, Darius Acuff Jr. and the rest.

AJ Dybantsa's Original Draft Position: No. 1

As tempting as it is to fixate on Dybantsa's poor three-point shooting and underdeveloped floor game, one month is nowhere near enough of a sample to outweigh multiple years of pre-draft run-up that labeled him the top prospect in the 2026 class.

While there's no case to be made that he's the best player in the class right now, Dybantsa should still be regarded as the one with the highest ceiling.

His athleticism and size mark him as an ideal big-wing first option. He's shown the ability to generate his own shot. His physical tools hint at a player who could be an elite off-ball disruptor and individual shutdown defender.

If we check in again toward the end of the season and find Dybantsa is still hitting less than a quarter of his threes while turning the ball over as often as he logs assists, we can re-evaluate. For now, his early-season rough edges shouldn't distract from the size, scoring skill and athletic suddenness that earned him the top spot in the draft.

Yaxel Lendeborg's Original Draft Position: No. 11

No rookie has been better this season than Lendeborg, a physically forceful driver who is hitting nearly 40.0 percent of his threes and looks like a legitimate first-option scorer. He's got elite size, knows how to use it against smaller opponents and can't be contained by like-sized defenders on the perimeter.

Yes, Lendeborg is already 24, but that only matters if you're convinced everyone else in the class is going to reach the level he's currently at by the time they're that age. While it's certainly possible that several players picked ahead of Lendeborg in real life will become stars, it's important to understand just how effective the Golden State Warriors rookie has been so far.

Forget comparing him to his draft classmates. Lendeborg ranks among the top 20 in Value Over Replacement Player among all players aged 24 or younger in the entire league. Statistically, he's playing like a star right now. That should count for something when everyone we'll list after him (and the guy we listed ahead of him) may only speculatively reach that level sometime in the future.

While teams that drafted teenagers and 20-year-olds spend the next half-decade hoping their picks pan out, Lendeborg will continue playing like an All-Star.

Cam Boozer's Original Draft Position: No. 3

Boozer leads the class in total rebounds and ranks second in assists, validating his supporters' belief that his court vision, feel and savvy would allow him to make an instant impact in several areas.

No other rookie has logged a triple-double yet, something Boozer accomplished in just his fifth game.

Three-point shooting problems aren't worthy of concern, but Boozer's 45.0 percent shooting on twos is worrying. Underwhelming athleticism means he can't finish against the heft and length of NBA defenders. It's possible a fully perimeter-oriented role is in his future.

Boozer will play the entire season as a 19-year-old, which gives him more runway than almost anyone in the class. Even if his interior scoring never lives up to expectations, he'll make an impact as a facilitator and spacer for years to come.

Darius Acuff Jr.'s Original Draft Position: No. 7

If Acuff can produce massive scoring numbers with decent efficiency in an environment as corrosive as Sacramento's, imagine what he'd do for a moderately competent organization.

On track to post the highest rookie scoring average since Michael Jordan averaged 28.5 points per game over 40 years ago, Acuff is using his quick-twitch burst and deft handle to put up buckets in bunches. Nobody's going to do backflips over a 47.8 effective field-goal percentage, but you have to consider the degree of difficulty. The Kings might have the worst coach in the league. Nobody else on the roster is making things easier for Acuff.

It's a borderline miracle he's still standing, let alone averaging 25.5 points and 7.1 assists per game.

The Allen Iverson comps are unfair, but you've got to admit the skill and sheer willpower Acuff has shown in a brutally tough situation are a little Answer-esque.

Darryn Peterson's Original Draft Position: No. 2

Peterson found his scoring touch after a slow start, putting up at least 20 points in five straight games after failing to crack that mark in his first eight. Though he's been marginally more efficient than Acuff, Peterson has had the benefit of playing with superior talent and, perhaps relatedly, has not had to shoulder nearly as large a creation burden.

This improved stretch in mid-November has showcased Peterson's pull-up touch and broader shooting potential. It's hard to bet against him becoming the best pure shooter in the draft. The questions come in other areas—like defensive consistency and his ability to get all the way to the rim.

So far, Peterson is only taking 11.0 percent of his shots at point-blank range . He'll need to improve that to become a three-level threat.

Caleb Wilson's Original Draft Position: No. 4

Prior to suffering a fractured right hand against the San Antonio Spurs on Nov. 11, Wilson was mostly delivering on the elevated expectations he created with strong Summer League and preseason play. All the surprising perimeter skills he showcased held up, best exemplified on Oct. 30 when he went 6-for-11 from three and scored 23 points against the Boston Celtics.

Wilson's jaw-dropping athleticism also gives him disruptive qualities on defense. He led the class with 18 steals before he got hurt. His nine blocks tied for second.

Highly competitive, much more gifted as an on-ball weapon than his college career suggested and toting a defensive ceiling that rates among the highest in the 2026 class, Wilson remains a terrific prospect and can't slip any further than this.

Keaton Wagler's Original Draft Position: No. 5

With Acuff off the board, the Sacramento Kings have to settle for Wagler, who falls two spots from his real-life position.

Though Wagler hasn't displayed anything like Acuff's scoring chops while playing a significantly smaller role than most of the other guards who came off the board in the top 10, he still has enough potential to stick firmly in this range. With great size at 6'6", a tendency toward steadiness as a playmaker you don't see in most rookies and plenty of long-range shooting potential, Wagler could still emerge as the top 2026 draftee at his position.

The same struggle to finish inside the arc that plagues most of his backcourt rookie peers applies, but it's encouraging that Wagler has shown a real knack for drawing contact. Lendeborg is the only rookie with more free-throw attempts this year.

Aday Mara's Original Draft Position: No. 12

Thrust into a larger role than expected due to injuries, Mara is using the opportunity to build on a preseason surge that saw him hit 78.8 percent of his shots while flashing elite passing vision for a player his size.

The 7'2" Mara is running away with the rookie lead in total blocks, which you'd expect. He's hauled in the most offensive boards in the class despite ranking just eighth in minutes. Adjusting for playing time helps frame Mara's contributions more clearly.

He's currently sitting at 15.3 points, 10.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.9 blocks per 36 minutes. Mara's 63.3 field-goal percentage doesn't hurt either.

Unlike most rookie bigs with his thinner frame, Mara competes with an edge and isn't easy to push around. His tenacity underneath mixes well with scoring touch and great court awareness to create the potential for Mara to become one of the best two-way centers in the league. That outcome is a long way off, but it's visible enough to justify a climb up the re-draft board.

Mikel Brown Jr.'s Original Draft Position: No. 6

This mild slide for Brown could have been worse. The original No. 6 pick started his career with a pair of duds, then missed a blowout loss to the Pacers on Oct. 25 to manage a back injury—not the kind of careful treatment you'd expect for a typical 20-year-old.

Since then, Brown has been a consistent double-figure scorer and has shown improved ability to get to the foul line. The point guard doesn't have a true standout game yet, but he's produced four contests with at least 13 points and three assists. One major concern: Brown has made more than half of his field-goal attempts just twice all year.

Concerns about Brown's strength and scoring efficiency have proved legitimate so far, but you can also see the positives from his pre-draft scouting report shining through. Even in a tough Brooklyn environment, he's showcasing some slick passing and finishing through his first month of pro play.

Kingston Flemings' Original Draft Position: No. 8

If you were only basing the decision on what's happened this season, Flemings should have gone at least as high as his original No. 8 spot. Thanks to a selfless call by teammate CJ McCollum, the speedy guard is already a starter for the Atlanta Hawks and plays an integral role in the team's shot creation.

Flemings' quickness and motor have clearly translated to the NBA level. He's given Atlanta an on-ball option who can pierce the defense with a live dribble. A lack of size often makes it tough for Flemings to finish at the basket, but he'll develop craft as he progresses. For now, his spray-out passing adds plenty of value.

He won't put up 23 points, five assists and five rebounds like he did against the Miami Heat on Oct. 28 often, but knowing that kind of impactful production is in there helps Flemings' case.

He still has to slip a little because of the higher upside we've seen from Brown, Wagler and the deeper lottery picks (Lendeborg and Mara) who've leaped up the list.

11. Golden State Warriors: Meleek Thomas

Meleek Thomas' Original Draft Position: No. 34

Meleek Thomas wouldn't give the Dubs Lendeborg's size or superstar wing potential, but there's something undeniably impactful in the confident guard's game. An occasional starter, Thomas plays with legitimate swagger, fires away from deep at high volume and competes like a guy determined to show he should have been an actual lottery pick.

Ranking seventh in total points among rookies, Thomas has made multiple threes in all but two of his appearances this season. He racked up 20 points in 33 minutes in a 10-point win over Dallas on Nov. 11 and added 10 more points two nights later to run his streak of double-digit scoring games to five straight.

In many ways, Thomas has looked like the player Darryn Peterson was supposed to be.

12. Oklahoma City Thunder: Bennett Stirtz

Bennett Stirtz's Original Draft Position: No. 16

The reason Bennet Stirtz fell in the actual draft carries over a bit here. An older prospect at 23, the Iowa product's stellar numbers take a back seat to his perceived lack of upside. We're still moving him up on the strength of his elite three-point shooting (42.9 percent) and steady passing chops.

Thunder fans who had to watch their team lose out on Mara in the re-draft can at least take solace that they end up with one of their real-life gems.

There will be defensive matchups Stirtz can't handle. It's hard to imagine he would have gotten to play as much as he has were it not for the rash of injuries that hit OKC earlier in the year. But the 6'4" guard is using his opportunity to show he's more poised and experienced (hardly a shock) than many of his classmates who spent a few months in college and entered the league as teenagers.

13. Milwaukee Bucks (via MIA): Brayden Burries

Brayden Burries' Original Draft Position: No. 10

Bucks fans who worried that passing on Burries at his original draft slot would allow another team to swoop in can breathe a sigh of relief. Milwaukee gets its man three picks later than in reality.

If we'd done this exercise a month ago, when Burries was riding high as one of the breakout stars of Summer League, there's no way the Arizona product would have been available here. In fact, he might have had a case to crack the top five on the strength of his offseason work.

Reality sets in during the games that actually count, as Burries is playing and starting plenty, but having a very hard time putting the ball in the basket. He's at just 26.5 percent from long range through his first 14 games.

There's still more on-ball juice in his makeup than most suspected. Burries is already one of the better rebounding guards in the league. It's just harder to see him as the potential star he seemed to be in July.

Nate Ament's Original Draft Position: No. 13

Nate Ament's best stretches of play so far have measured up to those of just about anyone in the lottery. Though only in fits and starts, the 6'10" wing is showcasing star potential.

Most are familiar with his baptism of Walker Kessler, a play that underscored Ament's athletic gifts and length. Closer observers (and Bucks fans) are more likely to be aware of his impressively improved finishing around the basket and 41.0 percent shooting on corner threes .

The sooner he becomes a regular starter for the rebuilding Bucks, the sooner we'll get a sense of how seriously we should be taking Ament's flashes of brilliance.

Allen Graves' Original Draft Position: No. 19

Graves' 41.3 percent hit rate on threes at Santa Clara hasn't followed him to the pros, but his intangibles, nose for the ball and versatility certainly have.

The 6'9" forward has yet to log more than 20 minutes of action in any contest, but his defensive work and floor game are allowing him to make a real impact. Graves' clamp-down stop of Trae Young highlighted his mobility and anticipation. He recently harassed Jalen Brunson into a live-ball turnover.

Raptors fans have already watched him create plenty of extra chances with his anticipation and hustle on the glass.

Graves showed some on-ball verve as a creator in college. We've also seen some flashes of that in Toronto. Though not likely to become a star, the 20-year-old seems sure to be a reliable on-the-margins contributor who does the dirty work necessary to impact winning.

16. Oklahoma City Thunder (via MEM): Trevon Brazile

Trevon Brazile's Original Draft Position: No. 35

He doesn't quite make it all the way into the lottery, but Trevon Brazile is still one of the biggest re-draft risers at the one-month mark.

Offensively, the 23-year-old is carving out a niche by taking almost half of his shots from beyond the arc. That stretch dimension, paired with rugged offensive rebounding and a high-revving motor, makes Brazile a surprisingly easy plug-and-play big man. It turns out that if you can scare defenses from deep while playing extremely hard, rotation minutes are pretty easy to come by.

Brazile's top-notch athleticism also makes him a vertical threat on lobs. Combined with his hustle, it creates serious defensive impact. His 8.6 contested shots per 36 minutes rates second only to Aday Mara among rookies with at least 100 minutes of court time.

17. Detroit Pistons (via OKC and MEM): Morez Johnson Jr.

Morez Johnson Jr.'s Original Draft Position: No. 9

We're not drafting for need, but the Detroit Pistons could certainly use Johnson's physicality and rebounding with Jalen Duren missing time.

A 13-point, 17-rebound effort against Utah on Nov. 6 was Johnson's clear high-water mark, as he'd only reached double-digit points twice and had never hauled in more than six boards in a game prior to that breakout.

There's very little evidence Johnson has any stretch to his offensive game. He's a positional tweener at the 4/5. Those drawbacks, plus some ghastly inefficiency (1-for-10 against Boston on Nov. 15), mean it's possible a future re-draft could see the former Michigan star fall even further.

At the same time, it's still early enough for Johnson to prove that his physical strength and athleticism give him a higher ceiling than we're seeing now.

Sergio De Larrea's Original Draft Position: No. 25

There's a good case to be made here for Charlotte's actual pick at No. 18, Christian Anderson. That's particularly true if you're not swayed by Sergio De Larrea's four-game sample as a pro. A knee injury knocked him out on Oct. 26, and he hasn't played since.

In that early-season stretch, De Larrea averaged 16.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.9 assists per 36 minutes while outshooting Anderson from the field and from deep. Do with that what you will, but it seems relevant that De Larrea was billed as a passer and creator (which was clearly correct). He shot it more efficiently than Anderson, who was among the most highly regarded marksmen in the class.

It's early, but De Larrea's passing craft and facilitating flair were consistent through Summer League and the preseason. That they carried over into his brief start this year suggests they're for real.

Christian Anderson's Original Draft Position: No. 18

Anderson doesn't fall far, sliding one spot to land with the Toronto Raptors instead of real-life selection Allen Graves.

After seeing the floor for single-digit minute totals in four of his first eight games, the undersized, sweet-shooting guard is slowly carving out a larger share of backcourt playing time for the Hornets. He hit 10 of his 18 three-point attempts in a three-game stretch from Nov. 9 to No. 15, showcasing the pull-up touch that so intrigued draft evaluators.

If Anderson can survive defensively and tap into his pick-and-roll orchestration skills a bit more, he'll be a lot harder to keep off the floor. As it stands, the shooting-starved Hornets should probably feature him more often. Though not a perfect prospect, Anderson's last few games validated his value as a sniper.

Hannes Steinbach's Original Draft Position: No. 14

Steinbach is averaging 12.0 rebounds per 36 minutes. Nearly half of them are coming on the offensive glass. All the mobility and scoring-related questions attached to him during the draft process may turn out to be legitimate, but at least we know his billing as one of the best rebounders in the class is real.

It'll be interesting to see whether Steinbach dips his toe in the water as a spacer. He has yet to shoot a three in the NBA after getting up 53 and making 34.0 percent of them at Washington. Adding that dimension would go a long way toward helping the power forward establish himself as more than a board-hunting banger underneath.

So far, it looks more like Steinbach is ticketed for a small, relatively one-dimensional role.

21. Memphis Grizzlies (via DET): Ryan Conwell

Ryan Conwell's Original Draft Position: No. 37

Conwell joins Meleek Thomas and Trevon Brazile to make it three second-rounders who've climbed into the top 21. Thomas' stock rose on the strength of his scoring prowess and swagger, while Brazile's energy and rebounding helped him ascend.

For Conwell, it's all about the shooting.

After barely playing in October, Conwell butted into Miami's rotation by hitting threes with regularity. He was at 35.7 percent for the year before a cold night against the Rockets on Nov. 16. He is already being viewed as a threat by defenders. Toss in some secondary facilitation and the occasional three-steal outburst like the one he had against Golden State on Nov. 5, and you've got a pretty good explanation for why the real-life No. 37 pick is on the rise here.

Ebuka Okorie's Original Draft Position: No. 17

Draft pedigree tops on-court performance for Okorie, who can't fall any further than this despite barely seeing the floor this season.

Lightning-quick with a live dribble and routinely capable of getting to the rim throughout a high-scoring season at Stanford, Okorie is also probably a better shooter than his collegiate numbers suggest. A 35.4 percent hit rate from long range means more when a majority of them are self-created off the dribble.

Zubi Ejiofor's Original Draft Position: No. 23

Dailyn Swain is sitting right there on the list of available players, as the lone top-15 pick still without a team. But it's too hard to make the case that the Hawks (or anyone) would grab him ahead of Ejiofor based on the first month of the season.

While he's still too small to man the center spot on a full-time basis, Ejiofor is showing enough defensive versatility and rebounding prowess to earn minutes in Atlanta's frontcourt rotation. Only a tinkerer in college from beyond the arc, the 6'9" forward has gone from 3.0 deep attempts per 36 minutes last season at St. John's to 5.2 per 100 as a pro. It doesn't hurt that he's also hitting about half of his tries so far.

If that dimension of Ejiofor's game proves to be real, he'll probably move up in subsequent re-drafts.

24. Los Angeles Lakers (via NYK): Dailyn Swain

Dailyn Swain's Original Draft Position: No. 15

It's not a great sign that Dailyn Swain landed in the G League just a few weeks into his first season. Players picked in the middle of the first round—especially those selected by teams like the rebuilding Bulls—should get NBA reps (and take their lumps) as often as possible.

For what it's worth, the 6'7" wing averaged 17.5 points, 8.0 rebounds and 6.5 assists in two contests with the Windy City Bulls. Those numbers are encouraging, even if they came against lower-level competition.

Swain's slashing game, length, two-way potential and nascent playmaking got him selected at No. 15. We're not going to let a rough first month in the league completely erase those qualities. The Texas product has to fall a few spots, but he can't slide all the way out of the first round.

25. Dallas Mavericks (via LAL and NYK): Labaron Philon Jr.

Labaron Philon Jr.'s Original Draft Position: No. 22

A stacked, win-now Philadelphia 76ers team was never going to allow Philon to spread his wings, so the 20-year-old guard hasn't had a chance to validate his plusses or dispel concerns about his minuses in 5.2 minutes per game.

That means we have to trust in the rim pressure, shooting range and foul-drawing craft that made Philon the No. 22 pick in reality. It also requires us to remain skeptical about the willowy guard's ability to defend against NBA size and strength. Philon was neither disruptive off the ball nor impactful on it as a collegiate defender, which means he's ticketed for a bench role unless he proves he can run an offense as a lead guard.

He won't get that chance in Philly, but we shouldn't give up on the possibility that he could tap into his strengths elsewhere.

26. San Antonio Spurs (via DEN): Karim Lopez

Karim Lopez's Original Draft Position: No. 21

Karim Lopez's crafty driving game and surprising ball-handling skill for a 6'9", 222-pound bruiser intrigued the Grizzlies enough to take him at No. 21 in reality. Though an uncertain outside shot and a lack of burst give the burly wing a low floor, his potential as a downhill attacker and physical defender certainly makes Lopez worth a gamble five spots later.

Lopez occasionally resembles his rookie teammate Cam Boozer when you see NBL film of him handling on the perimeter and slow-stepping defenders around the rim. Though nowhere near as productive or skilled as the guy Memphis took with the No. 3 pick, Lopez shares some of the high IQ and pick-and-roll savvy.

We've seen next to nothing from Lopez with the Grizzlies, but the Spurs could use his unselfishness and strength.

Jayden Quaintance's Original Draft Position: No. 20

The offense is...well, who knows? But if Jayden Quaintance can ever get his knee healthy, he's got a chance to be the most overwhelming defensive force in the 2026 class.

Standing 6'9" with a 9'1" standing reach, the Kentucky big man has the tools and motor to dominate around the basket while also defending in space. Already weighing over 250 pounds at 19, the high-energy stopper won't be bullied by NBA size and would probably compensate with elite hustle even if he were overmatched physically.

It remains to be seen whether Quaintance will ever get healthy, rediscover the athletic explosiveness he showed in 2024-25 at Arizona State or do enough on offense to stick in a rotation. But the possibility that he will makes him worth grabbing before the end of the first round.

28. Brooklyn Nets (via MIN): Cameron Carr

Cameron Carr's Original Draft Position: No. 24

Whether he cracks an NBA rotation or not, Camreon Carr is going to be a household name at some point. His ridiculous athleticism and penchant for dunking on opponents will land him on highlight reels, whether he plays five minutes or 35 a night.

A 37.4 percent three-point shooter on 6.1 attempts per game in his junior season at Baylor, Carr might have more in his offensive bag than just dunks. The same length and burst that produced all those jams should also translate to defensive disruption.

Though Carr hasn't seen much action, he has enough on his college resumé to warrant a speculative pick here.

29. Sacramento Kings (via CLE): Bryce Hopkins

Bryce Hopkins' Original Draft Position: No. 49

Production is production. We've gone far enough in the draft to value Hopkins' hustle and reliable shooting over the upside of some younger alternatives.

The 24-year-old flashed real scoring talent when an injury-hit Denver Nuggets team gave him rotation minutes, including a pair of starts back in October. His best efforts included a 13-point outing against the Warriors on Oct. 26 and an 18-point night in a win over the Raptors on Nov. 4.

Minutes have been much harder to come by as Denver has gotten healthier, but Hopkins has already made a habit of using his high-energy drives and physical style to great effect when given the opportunity.

30. Phoenix Suns (via DAL and NYK): Baba Miller

Baba Miller's Original Draft Position: No. 36

Baba Miller isn't making a massive leap here, but it feels right to honor his recent strong performances with a move from No. 36 into the final spot of the first round.

The 6'11" forward put up 12 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks in 20 minutes against the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov. 8, making him one of two rookies to produce those five-category totals in a game this year. Boozer, selected third overall, is the other.

Miller has near-center size but flashes some guard skills and led Cincinnati in assists last season. He's absolutely a project, but it's been pretty easy to see his potential whenever the Clippers have given him enough minutes to catch a rhythm. A suspect shooter in college, all bets will be off (in a good way) if Miller develops a half-decent three-point stroke.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

Grant Hughes covers the NBA for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, where he appears with Bleacher Report's Dan Favale .

articles.title: Damian Lillard Reveals Advice He Gave Giannis Before Star's Trade to Heat from Bucks
articles.summary: Having landed back on the team he requested a trade from, Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard offered his perspective to Giannis Antetokounmpo when the two-time NBA MVP was on the verge of leaving the Milwaukee Bucks.
articles.body:
Having landed back on the team he requested a trade from, Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard offered his perspective to Giannis Antetokounmpo when the two-time NBA MVP was on the verge of leaving the Milwaukee Bucks.

"The grass isn't always greener on the other side," Lillard said of his advice, per ESPN's Jamal Collier .

The nine-time All-Star guard understood Antetokounmpo's exit was inevitable. The Bucks had hit a wall and needed a massive roster reshuffle in order to contend again. Still, playing anywhere outside of Milwaukee may not have the same feeling.

Everything Giannis Said After Bucks Game

"They're not going to always love on you like the way they will at home," Lillard said. "That's what I'm experiencing now."

The Blazers reached a similar point to the Bucks in 2023. They failed to make the playoffs for two straight years, and that led to Lillard's trade request. His two years in Milwaukee were forgettable from a team success standpoint.

Still, he doesn't regret pushing for the trade.

"It was an experience that I needed to have," Lillard told Collier. "... Playing with another great player like Giannis and joining a team that had the intention of going for it."

Antetokounmpo is only 15 games into his Heat tenure, and the team is bound to look a lot different when the front office has a full offseason to build around Giannis and Bam Adebayo.

It's too early to draw any broad conclusions about where Antetokounmpo's career will go from here. The emotions might also be a little too raw to discuss a hypothetical return to the Bucks.

In time, maybe that's something that's on the table.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Talks Late Technical Foul in Celtics' Loss to Jokic, Nuggets, 'That's On Me'
articles.summary: Boston Celtics star forward Jayson Tatum expressed regret over a late technical foul that dashed his team's comeback hopes in a 105-101 road loss to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics star forward Jayson Tatum expressed regret over a late technical foul that dashed his team's comeback hopes in a 105-101 road loss to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday.

After Nuggets guard Jamal Murray hit a jumper with 6.4 seconds left to extend the Denver lead to three, Tatum tossed the ball in the direction of a referee who wasn't looking rather than handing it to the ref closest to him:

Tatum was assessed a technical foul as a result, allowing Murray to hit what was essentially the game-clinching free throw, giving the Nuggets a four-point lead with seconds remaining.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Tatum admitted that he should have handled the situation differently, saying, "I should have just probably gave the ball to the ref closest to me. Whatever I thought that John [Goble] was looking at our bench, I should have just found the guy closest to me—the ref closest to me—and just gave him the ball. So that's on me."

Tatum went on to note that while there was no malice behind the ball toss, he could have taken a simpler approach, saying, "I told [referee] Eric [Dalen], I was like, 'I wasn't mad. It wasn't a foul on me.' We just called timeout. John Goble called timeout and pointed at our bench. I thought he was looking at this way, but, yeah—they called a tech. So, for me, just find the female ref [Chelisa Painter] that was there or the other ref and whoever was probably closest and should have just gave him the ball."

Prior to the game's controversial ending, it was a back-and-forth affair between two of the NBA's best teams.

Boston led by 12 at halftime, but Denver stormed back to tie it entering the fourth quarter, and did just enough in the final frame to hang on.

As is so often the case, three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokić was the engine behind Denver's success Wednesday, scoring a team-high 24 points to go along with nine assists and eight rebounds.

Tatum matched Jokić's 24 points, adding eight rebounds and three assists, but he also turned the ball over six times and was responsible for the costly tech.

The loss marked Boston's second in a row on the heels of a six-game winning streak, but the Celtics are still second in the Eastern Conference with an 11-4 record, just 1.5 games behind the 13-3 Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.title: New Dejounte Murray Trade Rumors on 'Negative-Value Contract,' Potential Deal Structure
articles.summary: NBA teams reportedly aren't expected to jump at the opportunity to acquire disgruntled guard Dejounte Murray in a trade with the New Orleans Pelicans.
articles.body:
NBA teams reportedly aren't expected to jump at the opportunity to acquire disgruntled guard Dejounte Murray in a trade with the New Orleans Pelicans.

According to The Athletic's Christian Clark , there is a sense within the league that Murray is viewed as a "negative-value contract" due to the fact that he has a $32.8 million salary this season and a $30.8 million player option for next season.

Because of that, Clark theorized that the Pelicans may have to offer a draft pick or multiple draft picks along with Murray in order to entice a team to take on the remainder of his deal.

Fischer: Heat, Suns Linked to Dejounte 🔗

Last week, the Pelicans announced that Murray's agent, Rich Paul, had informed the organization that he wanted to be traded.

The Pelicans noted in a statement that they would "evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."

Murray, 30, has not appeared in a game since Nov. 11, and his on-court has been a major issue in recent years.

Over his three seasons in New Orleans, Murray has appeared in a total of just 54 games. A torn Achilles limited him to 31 games in 2024-25 and 14 games the following season, and he has played in nine games so far this season.

Prior to arriving in a trade in 2024, Murray spent six seasons with the San Antonio Spurs and two with the Atlanta Hawks.

He was an NBA All-Defensive Second Team selection with the Spurs in 2018 and followed that up four years later with his first and only All-Star nod.

Playing his final season in San Antonio, Murray averaged 21.1 points and a career-high 9.2 assists, 8.3 rebounds and 2.0 steals in what was his most productive campaign.

Murray averaged over 20 points per game in each of his two seasons with the Hawks, but he has not enjoyed that same success as a member of the Pels.

Over three seasons in New Orleans, Murray is averaging 16.6 points per game on just 41.9 percent shooting to go along with 6.6 assists, 5.9 rebounds and 1.9 steals.

Despite his lack of scoring efficiency and his durability concerns in recent years, Murray is still capable of filling up the stat sheet.

That could still make him a valuable addition for a contending team, but as Clark alluded to, the Pelicans may have to sweeten the pot to incentivize a team to assume the risks that come along with him.

articles.title: Iowa State's Sienna Harvey defends suspended head coach Bill Fennelly: 'He loves us and cares about us more than anyone'
articles.summary: Fennelly was suspended one game for shoving Harvey in the head during a timeout.
articles.body:
Sienna Harvey defended Iowa State head coach Bill Fennelly after he was suspended one game for shoving the guard in the head during a timeout.

"Obviously all of us like to be coached hard. We all have a great relationship with our coach," Harvey said Wednesday . "I can see how it was perceived on the Internet. But, he loves us and cares about us more than anyone. And I like being coached hard. It was just perceived differently to what it was."

The incident occurred late in the second half of Sunday's win over UIC . Fennelly yelled at Harvey in a huddle during a timeout, and he lightly shoved her in the head. Harvey didn't appear to react much in the moment, and Fennelly continued on as if nothing had happened.

Fennelly was suspended one game by the university for "inappropriate contact." Associate head coach Caroline McCombs was in charge for Wednesday's 72-57 win over Northern Iowa as the Cyclones improved to 6-0.

Following the incident, Fennelly issued a statement apologizing to Harvey .

"I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game," Fennelly said. "I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. "I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward."

"I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game," Fennelly said. "I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way.

"I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward."

Fennelly is in his 32nd season at Iowa State. He's led the Cyclones to the NCAA tournament 24 times, including in each of the last four seasons. He is 661-335 in Ames.

In October, Fennelly announced that he would be retiring after the season.

The Cyclones next play on Sunday at home against Drake.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards Opens Up on Knee Injury, Timeline to Return in 1st Comments Since Surgery
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves star guard Anthony Edwards spoke to the media on Thursday for the first time since undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his right knee.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves star guard Anthony Edwards spoke to the media on Thursday for the first time since undergoing arthroscopic surgery on his right knee.

Edwards told reporters that his timeline to return remains uncertain, saying, "I plan on coming back, but I don't know when."

"I never wanted to have surgery," he added . "Like, I thought it would just go away. But in the offseason, it was actually good… Then it flared up real bad."

Edwards appeared in just four games this season before being forced to undergo surgery last month. ESPN's Shams Charania reported at the time that he was expected to miss up to two months. He had dealt with runner's knee in the same leg last season, sitting out a career-high 21 games, nine of which came in the final 22 regular-season games to manage the injury. He later suffered a hyperextended left knee during the team's first-round playoff series.

Before being sidelined this season, Edwards appeared to be in top form. He opened the year with a 45-point, 10-rebound performance in a win over the Miami Heat. In his final game before going down, he dropped 47 points in an overtime loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Despite Edwards' absence, the Timberwolves haven't skipped a beat and rank first in the Northwest Division with an 11-4 record. The team has won seven of its last eight games entering Thursday night's matchup against the New York Knicks (8-6).

Minnesota will be hoping to get Edwards back in the lineup at some point, but with the lack of clarity surrounding his return, it will have to continue forging ahead in the competitive Western Conference without its top star.

articles.title: WNBA's Sparks Reportedly Nearing Record Sale to Padres Owners amid Vanessa Bryant, Pau Gasol Links
articles.summary: José E. Feliciano and wife Kwanza Jones are working toward an agreement to purchase the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks for $750 million, according to Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen.
articles.body:
José E. Feliciano and wife Kwanza Jones are working toward an agreement to purchase the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks for $750 million, according to Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen .

The price would more than double the record paid for a WNBA franchise, which Tilman Fertitta set when he bought the Connecticut Sun.

Tom Friend of Sports Business Journal reported Wednesday that Hall of Famer Pau Gasol and Vanessa Bryant, wife of the late Kobe Bryant, were part of a different group aiming to buy the Sparks. Bryant refuted the rumor on social media.

This adds to the sports portfolio of Feliciano and Jones, who assumed control of the San Diego Padres this summer in a $3.9 billion deal.

The Sparks are one of the WNBA's marquee franchises. They've won three champions and competed in the league's first-ever game in 1997. Nneka Ogwumike, Candace Parker, Lisa Leslie and Chelsea Gray are among the legendary figures who have donned purple and gold.

Feliciano and Jones are taking over at a point when L.A. is at a competitive nadir, though. The Sparks have had a losing record for six straight seasons, and they've cycled through three full-time head coaches during that span.

A 16-28 finish and the midseason trade of Kelsey Plum points to another rebuild. Ariana Andonian took over as the new general manager in September, replacing Raegan Pebley, and the team remains without a head coach.

Given who's available in free agency , an immediate turnaround is unlikely. The Sparks already have a sizable chunk of the salary cap tied up in the pair of Ariel Atkins and Dearica Hamby as well.

The fanbase will settle for having Feliciano and Jones lay out a clear vision for the future, one that sees Los Angeles contending for WNBA titles again.

articles.title: Dylan Harper Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Spurs Star's Timeline to Return amid Hip Strain
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper did not suffer a "major injury" after falling on the court Tuesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper did not suffer a "major injury" after falling on the court Tuesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday.

Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain that is expected to sideline him for one to three weeks, Charania reported.

Harper slipped and landed on his left side before limping off the court late in Tuesday's loss at the Detroit Pistons.

He had already been ruled out for Thursday night's home game against the Los Angeles Clippers due to what the Spurs described as "left hip soreness."

Harper was scheduled to undergo testing Wednesday. Spurs forward Julian Champagnie said during Thursday's shootaround he was happy Harper's injury was not "as serious as it could have been," per Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News.

Orsborn also reported Harper had been spotted at Thursday's shootaround "walking without a limp."

A one-week absence would sideline Harper for four games starting with Thursday's matchup against the Clippers.

Sitting out three weeks would cause him to miss his team's next eight contests, including upcoming NBA Cup matchups at the Portland Trail Blazers (Nov. 25) and against the visiting Los Angeles Lakers (Nov. 27).

Harper has ranked second only to Victor Wembanyama for the team scoring lead so far this season by averaging 18.4 points while plaing a team-high 31.7 minutes per game during the Spurs' 12-3 start to the season.

San Antonio could in his absence slot Champagnie back into the starting five of Stephon Castle, De'Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell and Wembanyama the team deployed throughout their run to the 2026 NBA Finals.

"We played a lot of minutes together last year, so I think we'll be just fine figuring out how to get the continuity going again," Champagnie said, per Osborn.

Fox and Vassell have both missed some time this fall, but the Spurs have spent most of the season so far with their full starting lineup available.

Head coach Mitch Johnson will now be tasked with helping his team adjust to the first significant rotational shift of the season as the Spurs continue battling the Lakers and Houston Rockets for the top spot in the West, starting with Thursday's 8 p.m. ET tip-off against the visiting Clippers.
